A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) the Mielnik succession is a valuable reference for the Campanian, (2) it contains a well-preserved calcitic cement that can be used for the study of early diagenesis and (3) the isotopic compositions of the belemnite rostral material are in agreement with those from the Lagerdorf, but not with the stratigraphic positions of some biozones in the GTS 2012.
the C isotope composition of the Mielnik chalk is similar to those of the other European epicontinental chalk deposits, while the O isotope composition is slightly more positive.
the Mielnik chalk section is a good candidate for the reference section for Upper Cretaceous marine deposits of the epicontinental seas in Europe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bulk rock δ 13 C is a useful tool for stratigraphy, but it is not an ideal proxy for paleotemperature.
the Mielnik belemnite assemblage can be used as a reliable biostratigraphical marker for the upper Campanian.
